toolChanges.reason: Redundant JS/TS linter — the project has zero authored JS/TS files (its only JS file is vendored third-party code, now excluded); ESLint9 alone covers the negligible remaining surface.
Had 0 patterns enabled on Cloud already (effectively inert) and is redundant with markdownlint for Markdown linting.
Wrong stack — no .ps1 PowerShell files exist anywhere in the repository despite Powershell appearing in GitHub's language detection.
Upgraded to ESLint9 — no project eslint config file constrains the version, so the newer major version was selected. The only JS file it would touch (vendored graphiql.js) is now excluded anyway.

Modern Python linter covering performance/security/best-practice concerns Pylint's defaults don't (PEP 585/604 annotations, blind-except, datetime.UTC misuse, etc.). Runs via pyproject.toml (no [tool.ruff] section exists, so Ruff's own defaults apply) — see localConfigTools.
Dependency vulnerability (SCA) scanning — found real CVEs in requirements.txt, including unpatched Django versions (3 High/Critical).

Broad Python/Django/YAML security and correctness scanning (CSRF, XSS escaping, MD5 usage, insecure random, missing request timeouts, unpinned GitHub Actions). One bogus pattern removed and test directories excluded — see patternChanges/fileExclusions.
IaC and OpenAPI security scanning (Dockerfile, GitHub Actions, OpenAPI schema secrets).
Adds cyclomatic-complexity and function-length metrics, a gap in the previous tool set.
Adds SQL linting coverage for the repo's committed .sql file. Currently 0 issues because the one large seed-data file exceeds the default parse-size limit, not because it's unused.

patternChanges.reason: Enforces a 'RAC_* table naming' rule from an unrelated organization's coding standard — not applicable to this project. Produced 408 false positives, one for nearly every statement in data/Initial Data Load.sql. Largest single noise source found.

100% overlaps Pylint's own docstring rules (C0114/C0115/C0116) and contradicts the project's own .configs/.prospector.yaml, which explicitly sets doc-warnings: false. Would have produced 744 duplicate/unwanted findings.

Duplicates the dedicated Bandit tool's coverage of the same B-codes, but ignores the project's pyproject.toml [tool.bandit] exclude_dirs for test fixtures — the dedicated Bandit tool respects that convention and is kept instead. Would have produced 110 duplicate findings.
Every one of its 38 findings (all E501 line-too-long) was a strict subset of Pylint's own C0301 line-length findings at the same file/line — zero unique signal.

deduplication: Prospector_bandit disabled — same B-code security concerns remain covered by the dedicated Bandit tool, which additionally respects the project's own test-directory exclusions that Prospector's bundled bandit check ignores.
newCoverage: Semgrep security/correctness findings (27 issues after tuning: missing CSRF token, unescaped Django template XSS, MD5 usage, insecure random, missing request timeout, unpinned GitHub Actions SHAs)
Trivy dependency vulnerability scanning (27 issues: 3 High/Critical unpatched Django CVEs in requirements.txt)
Checkov IaC/OpenAPI security scanning (3 issues after generated-schema exclusion)
noisyButKept: Semgrep hashicorp-tf-password secret-detection pattern kept fully active — only excluded for test directories (applications/API/tests, applications/graphQL/tests, applications/frontend/tests, common/tests, core/tests) that contain known dummy fixture passwords like 'pass1234', matching the project's existing pyproject.toml [tool.bandit] exclude_dirs convention exactly.

keyImprovements: Removed a bogus Semgrep rule enforcing an unrelated organization's 'RAC_* table naming' policy that produced 408 false positives against a SQL seed-data file — the single largest noise source in the repository.

Excluded auto-generated, timestamped OpenAPI schema snapshots (schema/schema*.yaml, produced by the Taskfile's `spectacular` dump task) — eliminated 175 stale-documentation issues (100% of Spectral's findings, most of Checkov's OpenAPI findings) with zero loss of real coverage.

Deduplicated Prospector's docstring, line-length, and bandit sub-checks against Pylint and the dedicated Bandit tool, removing 892 redundant findings while keeping every concern covered by the more precise tool.
Added 5 new tools (Ruff, Semgrep, Trivy, Checkov, Lizard), adding dependency-CVE scanning, broader Python/Django security coverage, and complexity metrics that were previously entirely missing.

Excluded a vendored third-party JS file (graphene_django's bundled GraphiQL UI script) that accounted for 100% of Biome and ESLint findings, and removed Biome/PSScriptAnalyzer/remark-lint as redundant or wrong-stack tools.

Excluded test directories from Semgrep's secrets scanner to match the project's existing Bandit convention, removing 7 false positives on dummy test-fixture passwords while keeping the scanner active everywhere else.

localConfigTools.note: Governed entirely by pyproject.toml, which has no [tool.pylint] section — so pure Pylint defaults apply (very strict on docstrings, naming, and line length at 100 chars). This is the dominant source of issues (67% of the total after tuning) and cannot be tuned via Codacy patterns; add a [tool.pylint] section to pyproject.toml to relax it.

Governed by pyproject.toml, which has no [tool.ruff] section — Ruff's own default rule set applies. Includes 24 confirmed false positives (Ruff_EXE001/EXE005 'shebang' rules misfiring on the project's `#!SECTION` comment-region markers in core/settings.py). Not fixable via Codacy config; add `[tool.ruff] extend-ignore = ["EXE001", "EXE005"]` to pyproject.toml to fix.

Governed by the existing [tool.bandit] section (skips B101, excludes test directories) — working as intended and producing real findings (e.g. requests without timeout, insecure temp file usage, non-cryptographic random).

On Codacy Cloud, Prospector already runs in local-configuration-file mode and correctly picks up .configs/.prospector.yaml (including its pylint_django-aware pylint sub-check, 81 findings) — the Cloud import correctly rejected (409) an attempt to switch it to Codacy-managed patterns. Locally, the Analysis CLI could not resolve this non-default config path (produced 0 issues even with the path set explicitly), so the local config uses explicit managed patterns instead, minus the patterns that duplicated Pylint/Bandit. Cloud and local Prospector behavior intentionally differ for this reason.

errors.detail: Unable to update Project Tool Patterns, repository is using a Configuration File. Resolved manually afterward via `codacy tool SQLFluff --enable`.

Unable to update Project Tool Patterns, repository is using a Configuration File. Investigated and left as-is deliberately — see localConfigTools; Cloud's existing local-config setup for Prospector is correct and should not be overridden.

warnings: First import attempt (without --force) also failed on Biome and ESLint8 with 'Cannot disable a tool that is enabled by a standard' (2 errors) — resolved by retrying with --force after user confirmation.

Unlinking the 'Standard' Coding Standard caused Codacy to auto-enable 2 tools never requested (PMD, TSQLLint) as an apparent fallback default — both were wrong-stack (no Java/Apex, no T-SQL) and were disabled manually via `codacy tool <name> --disable`.

The new file exclusions (schema/schema*.yaml, static/graphene_django/graphiql.js, Semgrep test-dir excludes) do NOT yet apply on Codacy Cloud — Cloud only reads .codacy.yaml from the repository's default branch (master), and this file currently only exists uncommitted on the feat_adds_loki_log_handler branch. Confirmed via post-import Cloud overview: spectral_operation-description and spectral_oas3-valid-media-example (both scoped to schema/schema*.yaml) still show 25 issues each. Exclusions will take effect once .codacy.yaml is committed and merged to master.

Issue count rose (923 → 1381) primarily because 5 new tools with real, previously-uncovered findings went live (Semgrep, Trivy, Checkov, Lizard, plus ESLint9's fuller ruleset) — not a regression in tuning quality.
Post-import overview still shows the full 175 schema/schema*.yaml-scoped issues (Spectral + Checkov) because .codacy.yaml has not been committed to master yet (see importResults.warnings).

Prospector_pylint (81 issues) appears in the post-import overview — this is Cloud correctly running the project's own .configs/.prospector.yaml (with its pylint_django plugin), not leftover noise; see localConfigTools.
